historical_record.description: A building contract was recorded for ornamental iron, bronze work, doors, iron stairways, elevator cars and skylight guards for a two-storey and three-storey Class A building. C. E. Gottschalk was named as architect and the California Artistic Metal & Wire Co. as contractor. The owner was the First National Bank of San Francisco.

A building contract was recorded for interior and exterior painting, decorating and tinting for a two and three-storey Class A building with a basement. C. E. Gottschalk was named as architect and the J. H. Keefe Co. as contractor. The owner was the First National Bank of San Francisco.

A building contract was recorded for grading, excavating, bulkheading and shoring for an addition to the building, at $5,790. C. E. Gottschalk was named as architect and J. P. Holland as contractor. The owner was the First National Bank of San Francisco.

A building contract was recorded for plate glass, wire plate glass, moss glass and glazing for a two and three-storey Class A building of offices and bank, at $17,000. C. E. Gottschalk was named as architect and Fuller & Goepp as contractors. The owner was the First National Bank.

A building contract was recorded for sheet metal work for a two and three-storey Class A building. C. E. Gottschalk was named as architect and the United States Metal Products Co. as contractor. The owner was the First National Bank of San Francisco.

C. E. Gottschalk's plans for the First Federal Trust Company and the First National Bank put the two-storey Class A bank and office building on foundations heavy enough for ten more floors, at an estimated $300,000.
